findings.summary: The assembly series is not visible as its own series after the first batch size. The assembly is plotted solid mauve #b279a2 with a circle at zorder 4 (:20) and the booking tangent dashed #2f6b5e with a square at zorder 5 (:18), every stage at the same markersize=7 (:56), so the later-drawn opaque square covers the circle wherever the two coincide. They coincide: 109.58 against 109.55 ms at 4 slices, 108.94 against 110.68 at 16 and 108.96 against 110.55 at 64, which is 0.1 to 1.6 px on this axis. Measured on the 1378x698 render, the assembly has 0 core pixels within +-6 px of the 4-slice marker column against 129 for the tangent, and 7 and 12 at the 16- and 64-slice columns against 127 and 121, a sliver at the square's edge; across its whole span the mauve ink reaches only 475 of 977 columns in 26 gaps longer than 10 px, so a reader sees an intermittent mauve hairline with no assembly marker anywhere after the first point, while the legend keys the assembly to a solid line and a circle. The reader therefore cannot check the assembly value at any batch size, which is the 111 ms the stage table and caption rely on to call the pair flat. This is the mirror of the defect the previous figure review blocked on (there the tangent was red #e45756, measured at 660 core pixels against 4012 mauve, with its markers covered): the colour changed and the draw order swapped, so the hidden series changed too. Drawing the assembly mark last, offsetting the two series, or giving the assembly a lightness step that survives overdraw would fix it without moving the data.

The orange LU factor line (#f58518) has a luminance contrast of 2.55:1 against the white background, below the 3:1 floor the repository's plotting rules set for a data line on white; the other five coloured series clear it (6.25, 4.61, 6.20, 3.16 and 3.41:1). The line remains findable because it is isolated in the 2-7 ms band, but it is the faintest mark in the figure and it fades on a projected or printed page.

The figure block holds two img elements with the same src, so the reader sees the same plot twice on the page, one directly under the other, with two different alt texts. The first alt omits the read series altogether, while the second describes it and names the series colours, so the page reads as two figures of the same data rather than one. One img should be removed.

The alt text says the booking tangent and its assembly 'stay near 109 and 111 milliseconds per slice at every batch size', but the plotted values at one slice are 121.18 and 125.31 ms (the run's own stage log), 11 and 13 per cent above the claimed figures, and both fall by about ten per cent between one and four slices before flattening. A reader checking the figure against the text at the 1-slice point finds numbers that are not on the plot.

The two in-place truncation annotations are set at fontsize=12, while the data-ink style and the repository's plotting rules put direct labels and legend entries at 14 pt. They are the smallest text in the figure and the only text explaining why a series ends early, so they are the least legible part of an otherwise clean rendering.

Both savefig calls pass bbox_inches='tight' (:116-:117), which trims the 14 x 7.2 in (1400 x 720 px) canvas to 1378 x 698 px. The figure is therefore 22 px narrower and 22 px off the repository's declared slide canvas, so the label sizes no longer land at their declared point size when the image is placed at the canvas size.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC per-slice-wall.svg legibility: fail. Six of the figure's seven series read at a glance on the log axes, but the assembly series cannot be read after the first batch size: the booking tangent is drawn over it with an opaque square of the same 7 px marker size, and the two values are 1.1 px apart, so the assembly's markers are erased and its line survives only in the tangent's dash gaps. One of the figure's stage series is not visible as its own series. Finding 1.
